title: The Four Great Beauties in Ancient China
synopsis: The Four Great Beauties of ancient China: Xi Shi, Wang Zhaojun, Diao Chan, and Yang Yuhuan.

fullText.simplified:
中国古代四大美女

    西施、王昭君、貂蝉和杨玉环被认为是中国古代的四大美女。她们到底有多美呢？民间流传着关于她们美貌的小故事。
    西施是春秋战国时期越国的一名洗衣女。有一天，她在河边洗衣服。水中的鱼儿看到她映在水中那美丽的倒影，忘记了游水，渐渐地沉到河底。于是，西施有了“沉鱼”的代称。
    王昭君是汉元帝时期的美女。当时，南北交战，汉元帝为安抚匈奴，让王昭君嫁给匈奴。王昭君含泪告别了自己的家乡。在去匈奴的路上，她拨动琴弦，奏起悲壮的离别之曲。天上的大雁听到这悦耳的琴声，再看到弹琴的美丽女子，忘记摆动翅膀，跌落在地上。后来，昭君“落雁”的故事慢慢地流传于民间。
    貂蝉是三国时期王允的养女。有一天，貂蝉在花园里拜月，忽然一阵风吹过，云把月亮遮住了。这被王允看到了。他为了宣扬他的养女长得如何漂亮，见人就说：“我的女儿和月亮比美，月亮比不过，赶紧躲到云后面去了”。因此，貂蝉也就被人们称为“闭月”。
    杨玉环是唐玄宗的贵妃。一天，她在花园里赏花，刚刚一碰花瓣，花瓣立刻合了起来。这个被一个宫女看到了，她到处说，杨贵妃和花比美，花都羞愧得低下了头。于是，杨玉环有了“羞花”的代称。
    慢慢地，“沉鱼落雁”、“闭月羞花”变成了两个成语。现在，人们经常用这两个成语来夸赞女子的美貌。所以，当你要夸赞女孩子的美貌时，不单单可以用“她很漂亮”，还可以用“她有沉鱼落雁之容，闭月羞花之貌”。
fullText.traditional:
中國古代四大美女

    西施、王昭君、貂蟬和楊玉環被認為是中國古代的四大美女。她們到底有多美呢？民間流傳著關於她們美貌的小故事。
    西施是春秋戰國時期越國的一名洗衣女。有一天，她在河邊洗衣服。水中的魚兒看到她映在水中那美麗的倒影，忘記了游水，漸漸地沉到河底。於是，西施有了“沉魚”的代稱。
    王昭君是漢元帝時期的美女。當時，南北交戰，漢元帝為安撫匈奴，讓王昭君嫁給匈奴。王昭君含淚告別了自己的家鄉。在去匈奴的路上，她撥動琴弦，奏起悲壯的離別之曲。天上的大雁聽到這悅耳的琴聲，再看到彈琴的美麗女子，忘記擺動翅膀，跌落在地上。後來，昭君“落雁”的故事慢慢地流傳於民間。
    貂蟬是三國時期王允的養女。有一天，貂蟬在花園裡拜月，忽然一陣風吹過，雲把月亮遮住了。這被王允看到了。他為了宣揚他的養女長得如何漂亮，見人就說：“我的女兒和月亮比美，月亮比不過，趕緊躲到雲後面去了”。因此，貂蟬也就被人們稱為“閉月”。
    楊玉環是唐玄宗的貴妃。一天，她在花園裡賞花，剛剛一碰花瓣，花瓣立刻合了起來。這個被一個宮女看到了，她到處說，楊貴妃和花比美，花都羞愧得低下了頭。於是，楊玉環有了“羞花”的代稱。
    慢慢地，“沉魚落雁”、“閉月羞花”變成了兩個成語。現在，人們經常用這兩個成語來誇贊女子的美貌。所以，當你要誇贊女孩子的美貌時，不單單可以用“她很漂亮”，還可以用“她有沉魚落雁之容，閉月羞花之貌”。

sentences.english: Xi Shi, Wang Zhaojun, Diao Chan, and Yang Yuhuan are considered the Four Great Beauties of ancient China.

sentences.pinyin: mín jiān liú chuán zhe guān yú tā men měi mào de xiǎo gù shi
sentences.english: So how beautiful were they?
Some stories of their beauty have spread among the Chinese people.

sentences.simplified: 西施是春秋战国时期越国的一名洗衣女。

sentences.traditional: 有一天，她在河邊洗衣服。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu yì tiān tā zài hé biān xǐ yī fu
sentences.english: Xi Shi was a laundry girl in the Yue state during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States period.

sentences.simplified: 水中的鱼儿看到她映在水中那美丽的倒影，忘记了游水，渐渐地沉到河底。
sentences.traditional: 水中的魚兒看到她映在水中那美麗的倒影，忘記了游水，漸漸地沉到河底。

sentences.english: One day she was laundering clothes by the river.

sentences.simplified: 于是，西施有了“沉鱼”的代称。
sentences.traditional: 於是，西施有了“沉魚”的代稱。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì xī shī yǒu le chén yú de dài chēng
sentences.english: When the fish in the water saw her beautiful reflection, they forgot how to swim and sank to the bottom of the river.
Since then, the term “sinking fish” has been used to describe Xi Shi.

sentences.traditional: 當時，南北交戰，

sentences.english: Wang Zhaojun was a beautiful lady who lived during the reign of Emperor Yuan of Han Dynasty.

sentences.traditional: 漢元帝為安撫匈奴，讓王昭君嫁給匈奴。

sentences.english: Back then, during the war between north and south, ..

sentences.traditional: 王昭君含淚告別了自己的家鄉。
sentences.pinyin: wáng zhāo jūn hán lèi gào bié le zì jǐ de jiā xiāng
sentences.english: .. the Yuan emperor had Wang Zhaojun marry one of the Xiongnu in order to pacify them.

sentences.simplified: 在去匈奴的路上，她拨动琴弦，奏起悲壮的离别之曲。
sentences.traditional: 在去匈奴的路上，她撥動琴弦，奏起悲壯的離別之曲。
sentences.pinyin: zài qù xiōng nú de lù shang tā bō dòng qín xián zòu qǐ bēi zhuàng de lí bié zhī qǔ
sentences.english: Wang Zhaojun left her hometown in tears.

sentences.simplified: 天上的大雁听到这悦耳的琴声，再看到弹琴的美丽女子，
sentences.traditional: 天上的大雁聽到這悅耳的琴聲，再看到彈琴的美麗女子，

sentences.english: On her way to the Xiongnu, she plucked the strings on her instrument and played a tragic song of farewell.

sentences.simplified: 忘记摆动翅膀，跌落在地上。
sentences.traditional: 忘記擺動翅膀，跌落在地上。
sentences.pinyin: wàng jì bǎi dòng chì bǎng diē luò zài dì shang
sentences.english: The wild geese in the sky heard the beautiful melody and saw the beautiful lady playing the instrument, ..

sentences.simplified: 后来，昭君“落雁”的故事慢慢地流传于民间。
sentences.traditional: 後來，昭君“落雁”的故事慢慢地流傳於民間。
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái zhāo jūn luò yàn de gù shi màn man de liú chuán yú mín jiān
sentences.english: .. and forgot to flutter their wings and fell to the ground.
Later on, the “falling geese” story about Zhaojun spread among the people.

sentences.simplified: 貂蝉是三国时期王允的养女。
sentences.traditional: 貂蟬是三國時期王允的養女。
sentences.pinyin: diāo chán shì sān guó shí qī wáng yǔn de yǎng nǚ

sentences.simplified: 有一天，貂蝉在花园里拜月，
sentences.traditional: 有一天，貂蟬在花園裡拜月，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu yì tiān diāo chán zài huā yuán lǐ bài yuè
sentences.english: Diao Chan was the adopted daughter of Wang Yun of the Three Kingdoms period.

sentences.simplified: 忽然一阵风吹过，云把月亮遮住了。
sentences.traditional: 忽然一陣風吹過，雲把月亮遮住了。
sentences.pinyin: hū rán yí zhèn fēng chuī guò yún bǎ yuè liang zhē zhù le
sentences.english: One day, Diao Chan was in the garden worshipping the moon.

sentences.simplified: 这被王允看到了。
sentences.traditional: 這被王允看到了。
sentences.pinyin: zhè bèi wáng yǔn kàn dào le
sentences.english: A sudden gust of wind came along, and the moon was covered by the clouds.

sentences.simplified: 他为了宣扬他的养女长得如何漂亮，见人就说：
sentences.traditional: 他為了宣揚他的養女長得如何漂亮，見人就說：
sentences.pinyin: tā wèi le xuān yáng tā de yǎng nǚ zhǎng de rú hé piào liang jiàn rén jiù shuō
sentences.english: This scene was seen by Wang Yun.

sentences.simplified: “我的女儿和月亮比美，月亮比不过，赶紧躲到云后面去了”。
sentences.traditional: “我的女兒和月亮比美，月亮比不過，趕緊躲到雲後面去了”。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de nǚ ér hé yuè liang bǐ měi yuè liang bǐ bú guò gǎn jǐn duǒ dào yún hòu miàn qù le
sentences.english: To brag about the beauty of his daughter, Wang Yun began telling people:

sentences.simplified: 因此，貂蝉也就被人们称为“闭月”。
sentences.traditional: 因此，貂蟬也就被人們稱為“閉月”。
sentences.pinyin: yīn cǐ diāo chán yě jiù bèi rén men chēng wéi bì yuè
sentences.english: “My daughter is more beautiful than the moon. The moon even hides itself behind the clouds”.
As a result, Diao Chan also became known as “hiding the moon”.

sentences.simplified: 杨玉环是唐玄宗的贵妃。
sentences.traditional: 楊玉環是唐玄宗的貴妃。
sentences.pinyin: yáng yù huán shì táng xuán zōng de guì fēi

sentences.simplified: 一天，她在花园里赏花，
sentences.traditional: 一天，她在花園裡賞花，
sentences.pinyin: yì tiān tā zài huā yuán lǐ shǎng huā
sentences.english: Yang Yuhuan was the highest-ranking concubine of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty.

sentences.simplified: 刚刚一碰花瓣，花瓣立刻合了起来。
sentences.traditional: 剛剛一碰花瓣，花瓣立刻合了起來。
sentences.pinyin: gāng gang yí pèng huā bàn huā bàn lì kè hé le qǐ lái
sentences.english: One day when she was watching flowers in the garden, ..

sentences.simplified: 这个被一个宫女看到了，
sentences.traditional: 這個被一個宮女看到了，
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge bèi yí ge gōng nǚ kàn dào le
sentences.english: .. the flowers immediately closed as soon as she touched their petals.

sentences.simplified: 她到处说，杨贵妃和花比美，花都羞愧得低下了头。
sentences.traditional: 她到處說，楊貴妃和花比美，花都羞愧得低下了頭。
sentences.pinyin: tā dào chù shuō yáng guì fēi hé huā bǐ měi huā dōu xiū kuì de dī xià le tóu
sentences.english: This was seen by one of the maids, ..

sentences.simplified: 于是，杨玉环有了“羞花”的代称。
sentences.traditional: 於是，楊玉環有了“羞花”的代稱。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì yáng yù huán yǒu le xiū huā de dài chēng
sentences.english: .. who started telling everyone that even the flowers were put to shame when compared with Lady Yang.
Hence, Yang Yuhuan got the name “shaming flowers”.

sentences.simplified: 慢慢地，“沉鱼落雁”、“闭月羞花”变成了两个成语。
sentences.traditional: 慢慢地，“沉魚落雁”、“閉月羞花”變成了兩個成語。
sentences.pinyin: màn man de chén yú luò yàn bì yuè xiū huā biàn chéng le liǎng ge chéng yǔ

sentences.simplified: 现在，人们经常用这两个成语来夸赞女子的美貌。
sentences.traditional: 現在，人們經常用這兩個成語來誇贊女子的美貌。
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài rén men jīng cháng yòng zhè liǎng ge chéng yǔ lái kuā zàn nǚ zǐ de měi mào
sentences.english: Slowly, “sinking fish and falling geese” and “hiding the moon and shaming flowers” became two idioms.

sentences.simplified: 所以，当你要夸赞女孩子的美貌时，不单单可以用“她很漂亮”，
sentences.traditional: 所以，當你要誇贊女孩子的美貌時，不單單可以用“她很漂亮”，
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ dāng nǐ yào kuā zàn nǚ hái zi de měi mào shí bù dān dān kě yǐ yòng tā hěn piào liang
sentences.english: Now, people use these two idioms to speak highly of those women who look beautiful.

sentences.simplified: 还可以用“她有沉鱼落雁之容，闭月羞花之貌”。
sentences.traditional: 還可以用“她有沉魚落雁之容，閉月羞花之貌”。
sentences.pinyin: hái kě yǐ yòng tā yǒu chén yú luò yàn zhī róng bì yuè xiū huā zhī mào
sentences.english: So, don’t just say that “she’s beautiful” whenever you want to compliment a girl about how good she looks.
You can also say “her looks make fish sink and wild geese fall, outshine the moon and put flowers to shame”.

raw.synopsis: The Four Great Beauties of ancient China: Xi Shi, Wang Zhaojun, Diao Chan, and Yang Yuhuan.
sentence_translations: The Four Great Beauties in Ancient China
Xi Shi, Wang Zhaojun, Diao Chan, and Yang Yuhuan are considered the Four Great Beauties of ancient China.
So how beautiful were they?
Some stories of their beauty have spread among the Chinese people.
Xi Shi was a laundry girl in the Yue state during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States period.
One day she was laundering clothes by the river.
When the fish in the water saw her beautiful reflection, they forgot how to swim and sank to the bottom of the river.
Since then, the term “sinking fish” has been used to describe Xi Shi.
Wang Zhaojun was a beautiful lady who lived during the reign of Emperor Yuan of Han Dynasty.
Back then, during the war between north and south, ..
.. the Yuan emperor had Wang Zhaojun marry one of the Xiongnu in order to pacify them.
Wang Zhaojun left her hometown in tears.
On her way to the Xiongnu, she plucked the strings on her instrument and played a tragic song of farewell.
The wild geese in the sky heard the beautiful melody and saw the beautiful lady playing the instrument, ..
.. and forgot to flutter their wings and fell to the ground.
Later on, the “falling geese” story about Zhaojun spread among the people.
Diao Chan was the adopted daughter of Wang Yun of the Three Kingdoms period.
One day, Diao Chan was in the garden worshipping the moon.
A sudden gust of wind came along, and the moon was covered by the clouds.
This scene was seen by Wang Yun.
To brag about the beauty of his daughter, Wang Yun began telling people:
“My daughter is more beautiful than the moon. The moon even hides itself behind the clouds”.
As a result, Diao Chan also became known as “hiding the moon”.
Yang Yuhuan was the highest-ranking concubine of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty.
One day when she was watching flowers in the garden, ..
.. the flowers immediately closed as soon as she touched their petals.
This was seen by one of the maids, ..
.. who started telling everyone that even the flowers were put to shame when compared with Lady Yang.
Hence, Yang Yuhuan got the name “shaming flowers”.
Slowly, “sinking fish and falling geese” and “hiding the moon and shaming flowers” became two idioms.
Now, people use these two idioms to speak highly of those women who look beautiful.
So, don’t just say that “she’s beautiful” whenever you want to compliment a girl about how good she looks.
You can also say “her looks make fish sink and wild geese fall, outshine the moon and put flowers to shame”.
